title: feat(spec)!: refuse an SLA escalateTo that no approver acts under, at registration
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbCSEueUJDFmeZ9eARPJvzQM)_

Fixes #25598

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: narrowed

The registration-time leg of the card, and its last. The runtime leg landed in PR #25600 (`2351c8d079`): on timeout, a `reassign` whose target resolves to no one keeps the slate and notifies it. This PR refuses, at registration, the targets whose shape alone proves they name no one.

## What changes

`ApprovalEscalationSchema.escalateTo` (`packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts`) was a bare `z.string()`. It now refuses a value starting with `team:`, `department:`, `org_membership_level:` or `role:` (after trimming, as the runtime trims it), under every escalation action. The refusal is a `custom` issue at `escalateTo` that names the value, says why no one could take it, gives a per-prefix remedy, and lists what `escalateTo` accepts.

Measured on `main` `0a694821` before the edit:

- `approver-address.ts` (`plugin-approvals`): a person acts on a slot only under their user id, their email, or `position:NAME` for a position they hold (`actingAddresses`, `POSITION_ADDRESS_PREFIXES = ['position:']`). No approver acts under a `team:`, `department:`, `org_membership_level:` or `role:` literal.
- `escalateRequest` (`approval-service.ts`) reads `escalateTo` under `reassign` (new slate) and under `notify` (notice audience), so a dead literal names no one under either action. Under `auto_approve` / `auto_reject` it is unread. The refusal therefore does not depend on `action`.

What stays accepted: a user id, an email, a bare position machine name and `position:NAME`. Whether they resolve is directory state, and the runtime leg already judges it on timeout.

The refusal reaches every door that judges an approval node's config, by #21848's route: `FlowSchema.parse` (`defineStack`, `defineFlow`, `objectstack validate` / `compile`, the metadata save door) and the build judge `flowNodeConfigRefusals`, which reports `node-config-refused-by-contract` at `escalation.escalateTo`.

## The narrowing record (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3)

- **Changeset** `.changeset/25598-escalation-dead-target-refused.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **minor** (`Metadata-protocol: narrowed`), BREAKING banner, the Before / Now / Fix migration, and the ADR-0087 marker `registered approval-escalation-dead-target-refused`.
- **D3 semantic entry** `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.approval-escalation-dead-target-refused.ts`, modelled on `flow-approval-node-config-contract-refused`. There is **no D2 conversion**: which position or person a team, department or membership tier stood for is the author's call, and no value the platform could write would keep what the flow meant.
- **No tombstone**: no key is removed.
- **Dropped-refinements ledger**: a `.superRefine()` does not project into JSON Schema, so `automation/ApprovalEscalation` gains the site `escalateTo`, and `automation/ApprovalNodeConfig` gains `escalation.escalateTo`. The header totals moved with them (245 schemas, 840 sites). Projecting a prefix ban would need a new arm in `refinement-projection.ts`, which is a public-contract decision, so it is not done here.
- **Generated docs**: `content/docs/references/automation/approval.mdx` regenerated for the new `escalateTo` description.

## Tests

New `packages/spec/src/automation/approval-escalation-dead-target.test.ts`, 26 cases:

- §1: each of the 4 prefixes is refused at `escalateTo` under each of the 4 actions, and again when padded. The message names the value and `position:NAME`.
- §2: `usr_7f3a`, `vp@example.com`, `vp_operations` and `position:vp_operations` parse with the whole schema green and the value carried through. An omitted target stays absent.
- §3: `FlowSchema.safeParse` refuses each prefix at `nodes.1.config.escalation.escalateTo`. `flowNodeConfigRefusals('approval', …)` returns exactly one `node-config-refused-by-contract` at `escalation.escalateTo`. The four accepted shapes register.

Ablation at `dc70de62`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: `.superRefine(checkEscalationTargetShape)` removed (anchor 1 → 0, blob `585bcb51` → `039f25ea`). Result: 17 failed and 9 passed. Every refusal pin went red and every acceptance pin stayed green, as expected. Restored blob equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Verification (head `dc70de62`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test`: 724 files. The first run had one red, `scripts/dropped-refinements.test.ts`, because the ledger header still read 244. The totals were moved (`dc70de62`). On re-run, that file, the new file and `src/migrations` passed: 7 files, 284 tests.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: pass.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` and `check:generated`: all 14 artifacts current after `gen:docs`.
- Dogfood battery (owed by the `(narrowing)` arm), under `os-verify-lock`, at `dc70de62`: VERDICT command-exit 0. Test Files 296 passed, 3 skipped (299). Tests 2523 passed, 18 skipped (2541).
- `dispatch-gates --commands`: 114 derived families run at `dc70de62`, each exit 0 (exit codes captured before any pipe). `--ran` reconciliation: 114 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a derived zero). On the first sweep, seven gates refused with exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (no build output, or the teardown fixture missing from a shallow clone). Their prerequisites were built, or the fixture fetched, and all seven then exited 0. Every family CI runs is read from this PR's check-runs.

## Acceptance notes

- The runtime leg (#25600) still guards the timeout for a stored flow row registered before this landed, and for a dead target the shape cannot see (a missing user, an unstaffed position).
- `queue:` is the one other `type:value` fallback literal the approvals service can write, from the deprecated `queue` approver type, and nobody acts under it either. It is outside the card's four and is not refused here. It is reported to the seat as an open question.
- `skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md` describes `escalateTo` as "a position machine name … or a specific user id", which is still true. It is not edited, because `skills/**` is a governed surface.

Clause-② basis: nothing widens. The `(narrowing)` arm applies because `escalateTo` refuses values it used to accept. The claim's own `Clause-②:` line carries no arm, and the report names that difference.
